effects: A new record is created with a generated identifier, the submitted URL, a title, optional description and tags, the chosen collection or the default inbox, and creation time.
The record appears immediately in the library and in its collection's record count.
The record and its collection assignment are written to persistent local storage and remain after the application is closed and reopened.

failures.condition: The URL field is blank, is not an absolute address, or uses a scheme other than http or https.
failures.recovery: The owner corrects the URL and submits again, or cancels without creating a record.
failures.response: The save is refused and an inline message explains that a valid http or https URL is required; entered title and description are preserved.

failures.condition: The normalized URL already belongs to an existing record in the library.
failures.recovery: The owner opens the existing record, files it differently, or cancels the save.
failures.response: No second record is created; the product identifies the existing record and offers to open or move it instead.

failures.condition: Writing to local storage fails or is unavailable.
failures.recovery: The owner retries the save, exports nothing automatically, and can edit or cancel the pending form.
failures.response: The record is not reported as saved; an error message states that the library could not be updated while keeping the form values intact.

actions.name: Save a bookmark
preconditions: The owner explicitly invokes save, either from the library's primary add action or from a capture surface.
A URL is present and is an absolute http or https address.
If a collection is chosen, that collection exists in the owner's library.

effects: Edited title, description, tags, URL, or collection replace the previous values while the record identifier and creation time are preserved.

failures.response: The edit is refused with an inline URL message and the existing record remains unchanged.

failures.condition: The edited URL normalizes to a different existing record.
failures.recovery: The owner opens the conflicting record, keeps the current URL, or cancels.
failures.response: The edit is refused with an explanation that another record already uses that address, and the original record is left intact.

actions.name: Edit a bookmark's details
preconditions: The record exists in the owner's library.
The owner opens the record's edit surface with its current URL, title, description, tags, and collection populated.

effects: A new empty collection is created with a generated identifier, the trimmed name, and a creation time.

The new collection persists across sessions.

failures.condition: The supplied name is blank or contains only whitespace.
failures.recovery: The owner enters a nonblank name and retries.
failures.response: Creation is refused and the name field indicates that a name is required.

failures.condition: A collection with the same normalized name already exists, including the inbox.
failures.recovery: The owner chooses a different name or selects the existing collection.

preconditions: The owner supplies a collection name that is nonblank after trimming.

effects: The record's collection assignment changes to the target collection while its identifier, URL, metadata, and creation time are preserved.

failures.recovery: The owner refreshes the collection list, chooses an existing collection, or leaves the record where it is.

failures.condition: The record itself is no longer present in local storage.

actions.name: Move a record to another collection

The target collection exists and differs from the record's current collection.

assertions.given: The owner has a valid URL for a page they have not saved before.
assertions.negative: The save must not require a description, tag, or explicit collection, must not create more than one record, and must not store a copy of the page content.

assertions.when: The owner submits the save form with only the URL entered and leaves description, tags, and collection untouched.

assertions.given: The owner opens the capture form.
assertions.negative: No record may be created, no partial library entry may appear, and the form must not discard the owner's other input.

assertions.when: The owner submits with a blank URL or an address that is not an absolute http or https URL.

assertions.negative: A second record must not be silently created, and the existing record's metadata must not be overwritten by the duplicate attempt.
assertions.then: The product identifies the existing record and offers to open or move it, and the library still contains exactly one record for that normalized address.
assertions.when: The owner tries to save that address again.

assertions.negative: The record must not remain in the inbox after a successful save and must not be duplicated across both collections.
assertions.then: The record is created in the selected collection, appears in that collection's view, and its record is absent from the default inbox.
assertions.when: The owner selects that collection in the capture form and submits a valid URL.

assertions.given: A record exists with a title, description, tags, collection, and creation time.
assertions.negative: Editing must not create a replacement record, reset usage metadata unexpectedly, or lose the record's collection assignment.
assertions.then: The updated values are shown and persisted, the record keeps its identifier and original creation time, and collection counts reflect any move.
assertions.when: The owner edits the title, description, tags, URL, or collection and saves.

assertions.given: The library already has an inbox and may have other collections.
assertions.negative: A blank name or a case-variant duplicate must not create a second collection or silently replace the existing one.
assertions.then: A new empty collection with a stable identifier appears in the sidebar and collection pickers and persists after reopening.
assertions.when: The owner creates a collection with a nonblank name that does not collide after trimming and case folding.

assertions.given: A record is in the inbox and a user-created collection exists.
assertions.negative: The move must not duplicate the record, change its URL or creation time, or silently revert on reload.
assertions.then: The record leaves the inbox view, appears under the target collection, both counts change, and the assignment survives closing and reopening the application.
assertions.when: The owner moves the record from the inbox to that collection.

assertions.given: A record is displayed with a collection assignment.
assertions.negative: The record must not be left in an unresolvable collection and the library must not show a false success.
assertions.then: The move is refused, the record remains in its previous collection, and the owner sees that the destination is unavailable.
assertions.when: The owner attempts to move it to a collection that no longer exists in storage.

assertions.given: A saved record exists with a valid URL.
assertions.negative: The application must not navigate away from the library, render the page as its own content, or open a different URL than the one stored.
assertions.then: The original page opens in a new browser tab, the library remains in its current view, and the record's last-opened time and optional open count are updated.
assertions.when: The owner chooses open from the library card or the record detail.

assertions.given: A record exists whose external page cannot be opened or whose URL has become invalid.
assertions.negative: A failed open must not increment the open count, update the last-opened time, or remove the record from the library.
assertions.then: The library stays usable and the owner sees that the page could not be opened, with the stored URL still available for copying or correction.
assertions.when: The owner attempts to open it.

assertions.given: The owner's library contains records split across the inbox and one or more collections.
assertions.negative: Records from other collections must not be mixed into the result set, and selecting a collection must not modify any record.
assertions.then: The list shows only records in that collection, identifies the active collection, and keeps the active search and sort applied within it.
assertions.when: The owner selects one collection in the organization sidebar.

assertions.given: The library contains records whose titles, URLs, hostnames, descriptions, and tags differ from one another.
assertions.negative: Search must not be limited to titles alone, must not treat the query as case-sensitive, and must not return records the owner never saved.
assertions.then: The matching record is included in the result list, demonstrating case-insensitive substring search across all stated fields and the active collection.
assertions.when: The owner enters a word that appears only in a URL, hostname, description, or tag, with any casing.

assertions.given: The owner is viewing a collection with saved records.
assertions.negative: The product must not show unrelated records, silently broaden to another collection, or lose the query text until the owner clears it.
assertions.then: A no-results state names the active query and collection and offers to clear the search or change collection.
assertions.when: The owner enters a query that matches none of them.

assertions.negative: Sorting must not hide records, alter their collection assignment, or change the active search scope.
assertions.then: The visible result set is reordered consistently, records without usage values fall after those with values, and ties resolve to newest-added.
assertions.when: The owner switches between newest-added, recently-opened, and most-opened orderings.

assertions.negative: Metadata failure must not block saving, must not clear the URL, and must not create a record by itself.
assertions.then: The form remains open with the owner's values intact and a non-blocking notice explains the failure; the owner can type a title and save normally.
assertions.when: The external metadata service is unavailable, rate-limited, or returns no usable title or description.

assertions.negative: Renaming must not move records out of the collection, create a second collection, or allow the inbox to be renamed.
assertions.then: The collection displays the new name while retaining its identifier and all filed records, and the new name persists after reopening.
assertions.when: The owner renames it to another nonblank, non-duplicate name.

basis.statement: The product exists so a person can retain an external page they saw but cannot process now, and later find it again and return to the original page.

A bookmark manager is defined by four properties: records anchored to an external address, deliberate capture rather than automatic logging, a persistent accumulating personal library, and user-controlled organization and retrieval. The form of organization is an implementation choice.
The first actor step is an explicit save of a page the user wants to remember, made while browsing and without requiring immediate processing.
At save time the user may choose one simple category such as 待购, 家居改造, or 以后看看, and the user can create categories and move existing records between them.
An unsorted link may first enter a default category and be moved to a better place later.
When the user is ready to act, they open the personal library and locate the earlier link by browsing categories or by keyword retrieval, both scoped to records they already saved.
The final actor step is opening a record and returning to the original page to continue buying, reading, or referencing; the application does not take over content consumption.

At the pinned commit the README positions the application as privacy-focused and local-first, storing bookmarks in the browser IndexedDB with no accounts, servers, or tracking; the declared database is named BookmarkDB with a bookmarks table. This is static document and code evidence only, not a runtime claim.

The upstream Bookmark type contains id, title, url, hostname, favicon, description, tags string array, isPinned, isArchived, visitCount, createdAt, and visitedAt; it has no collection or folder field, no separate tag entity, no deletion marker, and no manual ordering field.

Upstream organization is tag-only: sidebar tag counts are aggregated from each record's tags array and sorted alphabetically, and no collection creation, naming, or move interface appears in the observed files.

The upstream search field matches only the record title as a lowercased substring; URL, hostname, description, and tags are not searched. Tag checkboxes are multi-select AND filters with a reset action, and the library is split into Home and Archived tabs.

Upstream save validation requires a valid http or https URL, a title of at most 100 characters, a required description of at most 280 characters, and one to five tags of at most 30 characters each; the URL input also hard-caps entry at 100 characters while the validation schema sets no URL length limit.

Upstream metadata retrieval is a manually triggered button that calls api.microlink.io for title, description, and logo, then proxies the logo through images.weserv.nl; failures are only logged to the console and the form remains manually fillable.
The upstream Visit action calls window.open with the record URL in a new tab using noopener and noreferrer; the card title is not itself a link, so opening requires the overflow menu.
The same Visit action sets visitedAt to the current time and increments visitCount before writing the record back to IndexedDB; no other observed action changes those values.

Upstream sorting places pinned records first, then applies the chosen strategy: recently visited by visitedAt descending, most visited by visitCount descending, with createdAt descending as the fallback and newest-added as the default.

Design proposal: organize the new product with one optional level of user-created collections plus a mandatory default inbox, because the scenario speaks of 归类, moving between 归类, and a 默认归类 while the upstream tag-only model cannot express an unsorted waiting area. Tags remain optional labels, not a second navigation structure.

Design proposal: require only the URL to save; derive the title from fetched metadata or the hostname, and leave description, tags, and explicit collection optional, because the scenario is about capture before processing. This deliberately relaxes the upstream requirement for a description and at least one tag.

Design proposal: persist the single-owner library in local browser storage and state explicitly that it is scoped to one browser profile. No account system is introduced, and cross-device synchronization is excluded rather than implied by the word persistent.

Design proposal: make opening the original page a directly visible primary action on the record and its detail view, not a hidden menu item, and keep the library open behind the new tab. Opening updates optional usage metadata but does not change the record's filing state.

Design proposal: search titles, URLs, hostnames, descriptions, and tags together, combine the query with one active collection, and default to newest-added ordering with optional recently-opened and most-opened orderings. This broadens the upstream title-only search because users often remember a domain or a phrase from the description.

Design proposal: prevent a second record for the same normalized URL and route the owner to the existing record, using trim, host lowercasing, and trailing-slash removal as the baseline. The upstream model uses a random primary key and contains no duplicate check.

Design proposal: treat metadata fetch as an optional, explicitly invoked convenience that discloses any third-party request and never blocks manual entry or saving. The upstream use of microlink and weserv is reference only, not a required dependency.

Design proposal: do not carry over the upstream field length ceilings or the 100-character URL input cap into the product definition, because they are implementation details unsupported by the scenario; the new product's limits remain open pending product confirmation.

Unknown: the pinned upstream application was not installed, built, launched, or operated in a browser. All upstream statements are static readings of five files, and runtime behavior such as real persistence, metadata-service responses, or interaction details is not established.

Unknown: the snapshot covers only LICENSE, README.md, src/App.tsrx, src/includes/store.ts, and src/includes/utils.ts. Missing package.json, entry modules, components, and styles mean the repository as a whole cannot be claimed to lack import/export, sync, sharing, trash, deduplication, tag management, or routing.

Unknown: the product does not yet define whether query strings and fragments participate in URL comparison, or whether different paths on the same host are distinct records. Only trim, host lowercasing, and trailing-slash removal are fixed as a baseline.
Unknown: no evidence establishes desired maximum lengths for URL, title, description, or tags, nor a maximum number of tags or records, so the new product imposes no such ceiling in the reference.

Unknown: success rate, rate limits, CORS behavior, response fields, and privacy impact of external metadata services (microlink, weserv, Google favicons) were not tested, and whether the new product should call any third party at all remains a product decision.

Unknown: expected library size, whether search needs an index, and whether pagination or virtualized lists are required have no source data; the core reference therefore specifies no pagination behavior.

Unknown: removal of saved links is not described by the scenario. The reference excludes deletion and trash from the core; if removal is later added it must be recoverable and clearly distinct from organization. Upstream permits deletion only for archived records and removes them immediately with a toast undo.

Unknown: the scenario requires persistence across sessions but does not confirm cross-device or cross-browser access. The leaf's broader category discussion mentions multi-device use, but this product boundary explicitly limits persistence to one local browser profile.

Unknown: interface language, date formatting, time zone display, and whether Chinese category names are examples only remain undecided; upstream strings are English and dates are hard-coded to the en-IN locale with day and abbreviated month.

Unknown: whether 待购, 家居改造, and 以后看看 should exist as first-run sample collections or be created by the owner is not settled. The design baseline starts with an empty library plus a default inbox and treats those names as examples, pending product confirmation.

gaps.resolution: Keep runtime behavior explicitly unknown; do not cite upstream as proof that persistence, metadata fetch, or any interaction works.
gaps.statement: The upstream snapshot records upstream_status and application_runtime_status as not_run: dependencies were not installed, the project was not built or started, and no browser interaction occurred. Every upstream observation is a static file reading and no execution result is claimed.

gaps.resolution: Scope claims are limited to observed files; product inclusion or exclusion is decided from the scenario and leaf, not from silence in the partial snapshot.
gaps.statement: Only five files are present at the pinned commit. The absence of a feature in those files cannot establish that the repository lacks import/export, synchronization, sharing, trash, duplicate handling, tag management, or routing.

gaps.resolution: Treat upstream as documentary evidence only; any implementation of this reference is a new build, not a claim that the upstream code runs.
gaps.statement: No package manifest, lockfile, entry module, or build configuration is available, and framework, styling, database, and validation version compatibility was not verified. Whether the pinned commit builds or runs is unknown.

gaps.resolution: Acceptance tests for this reference must perform a real close-and-reopen test in the target browser; until then persistence remains a requirement, not an observed upstream result.
gaps.statement: Persistence across reloads, browser restarts, private windows, and storage eviction is inferred from IndexedDB usage in the upstream code but was not tested. The new reference requires persistence while limiting it to one local browser profile.

gaps.resolution: Keep metadata assistance optional and non-blocking; test and disclose any chosen provider, or implement without third-party calls.
gaps.statement: External metadata and favicon services were not exercised; their availability, privacy implications, and failure presentation are unknown, and upstream exposes failures only through the console.

gaps.resolution: Baseline decision: start with an empty library and only the default inbox; confirm with the product owner before adding presets.
gaps.statement: Whether the example categories 待购, 家居改造, and 以后看看 ship as preset collections or are created by the owner on first use is not confirmed.

gaps.resolution: Model one collection per record plus optional tags; if multi-collection membership is required, the object model and move semantics must be revised.
gaps.statement: The scenario says 一个简单归类, which suggests one collection per record, but whether a record may belong to several collections is not explicitly confirmed.

gaps.resolution: Exclude synchronization from this boundary and state the local-profile limitation explicitly; revisit only if multi-device access becomes a requirement.
gaps.statement: The scenario requires persistence across sessions but does not confirm multi-device or multi-browser access. The leaf's category description mentions multi-device use, while the fixed product shape is a single-person accumulating collection.

gaps.resolution: Ship the baseline normalization for the core and record the unresolved comparison surface for product confirmation; do not add merge tooling.
gaps.statement: Normalization beyond trimming whitespace, lowercasing the host, and dropping a trailing slash is undefined; query parameters, fragments, and case-sensitive paths have no agreed treatment, and upstream has no deduplication logic to reference.

gaps.resolution: Render the loaded result set without pagination in the core; measure against a realistic collection and add performance work only when volume is known.
gaps.statement: Expected record counts, search latency targets, index requirements, and the need for pagination or virtualized rendering are unknown.

gaps.resolution: Treat the language as a product decision; avoid asserting locale-specific formatting in acceptance criteria until confirmed.
gaps.statement: Interface language, date and time formatting, time zone presentation, and the status of Chinese collection names as examples versus required labels are undecided.

gaps.resolution: Do not implement destructive removal in the core; if removal is requested, design a recoverable flow and keep it clearly separate from collection organization.
gaps.statement: The scenario does not describe removing a saved link. The reference excludes deletion and trash from the core, while upstream exposes deletion only for archived records with an immediate physical delete and a toast undo.

gaps.resolution: Impose no reference-level ceilings; validate only the URL scheme and shape, and set practical limits later from usability evidence.
gaps.statement: No evidence justifies limits on URL, title, description, or tag length, or a maximum tag count for the new product. Upstream's 100-character URL input cap conflicts with its own validation schema and was not behaviorally tested.

gaps.resolution: Treat usage metadata as optional supporting information; acceptance for the core depends on opening the page, not on statistics.
gaps.statement: Whether retaining open counts and last-opened times is acceptable is not confirmed. Upstream records both and sorts by them, while the scenario only asks to return to the page.

gaps.resolution: Keep tags as searchable free-form fields on records; exclude a tag sidebar and tag administration from the core boundary.
gaps.statement: Tags are preserved as optional labels from the scenario's evidence and upstream behavior, but whether tag filter checkboxes, tag counts, or tag management belong in the product is not confirmed.

journeys.completion: A deliberately saved link survives the session, is visible in the personal library, and can be reopened at its original address without the product recreating or hosting the page.
journeys.goal: Preserve a page encountered during browsing with almost no interruption, then come back to the live page when the owner actually needs it.
journeys.name: Save now, return later
journeys.recovery: If metadata fetch or favicon retrieval fails, the owner saves with only the URL and a derived title. If opening fails, the URL stays visible for copy or correction. If storage fails, the form remains populated and the save can be retried.

steps.success: The add action opens the capture form with the URL field ready and the inbox preselected.
With only a URL entered, the record is saved into the inbox with a hostname-derived title and appears in the library immediately.
The saved record remains listed in a later session, and opening it launches the original page in a new tab while the library stays open.

journeys.completion: The library's organization is entirely owner-defined, records can be refiled indefinitely, and collection assignments are durable rather than session state.
journeys.goal: Turn an unsorted accumulation into a personally meaningful structure by creating a collection and moving saved records into it, with the result surviving restart.
journeys.name: Triage the inbox into collections
journeys.recovery: If a collection name collides or is blank, creation is refused with an explanation and the inbox remains intact. If a move target is missing, the record stays where it was and the owner can retry from a refreshed sidebar.

steps.success: The owner opens the inbox and sees all records saved without an explicit collection.
A new named collection such as 待购 or 家居改造 is created empty and appears in the sidebar.
The chosen record moves from the inbox to the new collection and both counts update.
The owner adds a clarifying title or description without changing the record's identity or collection.
After reopening the application, the collection still contains the moved record and the inbox no longer lists it.

journeys.completion: The owner finds a record they already chose to keep and reaches the live resource; the product behaves as a retrieval tool for known references, not as a search engine for unseen pages.
journeys.goal: Locate a previously saved page from a remembered word, domain, or rough filing location and return to it.
journeys.name: Find a link remembered only vaguely
journeys.recovery: A no-results state preserves the query and active collection and offers to clear or broaden it. If the URL is broken, the record remains in the library with its stored address available for correction.

steps.success: A remembered word from the title, domain, description, or tag narrows the library to candidate records.
If several candidates remain, browsing the likely collection reduces the list to the relevant records.
The owner identifies the intended record and opens the original page, while the library retains the record for future retrieval.

fields.meaning: Stable internal identifier generated at save time; edit and move preserve it.
fields.name: id

fields.meaning: The absolute http or https address of the external web resource; the anchor that makes the record meaningful and the value opened when the owner visits it.
fields.name: url

fields.meaning: Owner-visible name for the record; may be fetched, may default to the page hostname when absent, and is editable at any time.
fields.name: title

fields.meaning: Optional free-text note describing why the page was kept; editable and never required to save.
fields.name: description

fields.meaning: Derived host portion of the URL, displayed to help recognition and included in search.
fields.name: hostname

fields.meaning: Optional reference to a small site icon, either fetched or absent; failure to obtain one never blocks saving.
fields.name: favicon_ref

fields.meaning: Optional free-form string labels attached to the record for recall and search; not a hierarchy and not a managed entity.
fields.name: tags

fields.meaning: Identifier of the single collection the record is filed in, including the default inbox.
fields.name: collection_id

fields.meaning: Time the record was first saved; never changed by later edits, moves, or opens.
fields.name: created_at

fields.meaning: Time the record's editable fields were last changed.
fields.name: updated_at

fields.meaning: Time the owner last used the record to open the external page; absent until the first open. Usage statistics are optional supporting metadata, not an acceptance requirement.
fields.name: last_opened_at

fields.meaning: Number of times the owner opened the record's external page through the product; optional supporting metadata and never a substitute for the URL.
fields.name: open_count

Held in the owner's personal library and subject to that library's persistence scope.

product_shape.audience: An individual web user who encounters pages faster than they can act — product pages, tutorials, documentation, inspiration, things to buy or revisit — saves them deliberately, and comes back weeks or months later to use them.
product_shape.boundary: One owner deliberately saves external web page URLs. Each record stores the URL plus minimal user-editable metadata, persists across sessions in the owner's local browser storage, and belongs to exactly one user-created collection or to the default inbox. The owner browses collections, searches their own records, and opens a record to the live page in a new tab. The library stores the reference and metadata only; page content remains on the web and is never consumed inside the application.
product_shape.delivery_profile: Single-user, local-first web application with one personal library per browser profile. No account, server, collaboration, or sharing in the modeled boundary. The upstream repository is read-only evidence at a pinned commit and was not built or run; no runtime behavior of that implementation is claimed.
excluded: Accounts, sign-in, identity verification, and multi-tenant access control
Collaboration, invited members, shared collections, and permissions beyond the single owner
Public profiles, public collection pages, social discovery, and follower networks
Cross-device or cross-browser synchronization; persistence is explicitly scoped to one local browser profile
Browser extension, bookmarklet, mobile share target, import from browsers or other services, and export
Preserved page copies, reader view, offline content archives, and read-later queues
Automatic capture of browsing history or any record created without an explicit user save action
Pinning, archiving, unread flags, reminders, and notes attached to records as core capabilities
Bulk edit, bulk move, and multi-select operations
Broken-link detection, link repair, and duplicate merge workflows beyond the save-time duplicate prompt
Deletion and trash in the core flow; removal semantics are an open product question
Full-text search over page content and search over anything other than the owner's own saved records
Tags as independently managed entities, tag hierarchies, or tag rename/merge administration
product_shape.name: Bookmark Manager — Personal Link Library
product_shape.value: A durable, private, growing library of references: every saved link is anchored to its live web page, can be filed into a simple user-defined collection or left in an inbox, and can be found again by browsing or searching so the user returns to the original page instead of searching the web for it.

roles.data_scope: All bookmarks, collections, tags, and metadata stored in this browser profile's local library. No other person's data exists in the product boundary, and no role can see or modify another person's library.
roles.goal: Save links with minimal friction, keep them organized in a way that makes sense personally, and find and reopen them later.
roles.name: Library owner

rules.statement: Records enter the library only through an explicit owner save or approved user-initiated import; the product never turns browsing activity into records on its own.
Every record is anchored to an absolute http or https URL; the record is a reference to content owned by the external site, not a copy of that content.

Saved records, their metadata, and their collection assignments persist across sessions in the owner's local browser storage; they are not confined to a single page session, and persistence is explicitly limited to that one browser profile.
The library always contains one default inbox; a save without a collection choice lands there, and the owner can later move the record into any collection or back to the inbox.
A record belongs to exactly one collection at a time; organization is a single-level, owner-controlled structure, while tags are optional free-form labels rather than a second hierarchy.

The library keeps one record per normalized URL: comparison trims surrounding whitespace, lowercases the host, and removes a trailing slash; a matching save is reported with the existing record instead of creating a second entry. Handling of query strings and fragments is not yet fixed.

Retrieval operates only on the owner's own saved records: search matches title, URL, hostname, description, and tags as case-insensitive substrings, and collection browsing narrows that same set; results never include pages the owner has not saved.
The default order is newest-added first; optional recently-opened and most-opened orderings apply only to the current result set and fall back to newest-added for ties so no record disappears.

Only the URL is required to save; title may be fetched or derived from the hostname, and description, tags, and an explicit collection choice are optional so capture costs seconds. Length ceilings for URL, title, description, and tags are not fixed by the evidence.

Opening a record launches its URL in a new browser tab with noopener and noreferrer semantics and leaves the library view in place; a successful open updates last-opened time and open count, while a failed open updates neither.

The library is private to one owner in one local browser profile, with no accounts, collaborators, public pages, or tracking; any third-party metadata request is an explicit optional action and must be disclosed rather than silently performed.

The product does not fetch, render, or persist the referenced page's正文 as a library object; there is no reader view, preserved snapshot, or read-later queue in the boundary, so the library guarantees the reference rather than the content.

Collection names are trimmed, nonblank, and unique after case folding; the default inbox is fixed and cannot be renamed or recreated as a user collection, so every collection is an unambiguous navigation target.

Organization is always revisable: a record can be moved or edited at any time, and renaming a collection preserves its records and identifier; the product never imposes a structure the owner did not choose.

scope_options.name: Core personal library
scope_options.rationale: The irreducible product: deterministic save from a URL, durable local records, an inbox plus owner-created collections, single-record moves and edits, collection browsing and cross-field search, and return to the original page. Everything here traces to the scenario or the leaf's defining core, not to upstream feature breadth.

scope_options.name: Optional metadata assistance
scope_options.rationale: Fetched titles and descriptions reduce typing but cannot be a save precondition; the scenario requires saving a link before deciding to process it. The slice must disclose any third-party request and leave manual entry fully usable when the service fails.

scope_options.name: Collection renaming
scope_options.rationale: A lightweight structural maintenance capability. The scenario only requires creating and moving, so renaming is a separable slice that must preserve record membership and the fixed inbox.

scope_options.name: Usage-based ordering
scope_options.rationale: Newest-added ordering is enough for a young collection; recently-opened and most-opened orderings help a large accumulated library. They are optional because the scenario asks for finding a link, not for sorting controls, and visit statistics carry unresolved privacy questions.

surfaces.name: Personal library
surfaces.purpose: Show the owner's saved records in the active collection, let them search, reorder, open, move, or start a save, and make the growing library feel navigable.

query.bulk: Not provided: selection, bulk move, and bulk edit are outside the core boundary.
query.export: Not provided and no export format is defined; interoperability is outside this product boundary.
query.filter: Exactly one collection at a time, including the default inbox; tag checkboxes and multi-tag AND filtering from the upstream implementation are not part of this boundary.
query.pagination: No pagination requirement is established; the record volume is unknown and the core renders the loaded result set in one scrollable list.
query.search: Case-insensitive substring match over title, URL, hostname, description, and tags of the owner's own records; an empty query applies no text filter.
query.sort: Newest-added descending is the default. Optional orderings are recently opened and most opened, each with newest-added as the tie-breaker.

sections: Top bar with product identity, search field, and primary add action
Active collection heading with record count and sort control
Record list or grid showing title, hostname, description, tags, collection, and dates
Per-record actions for open, edit, and move
Empty, no-results, and storage-error states

states.empty: No records exist: the view explains that saved links will accumulate here and presents the add action plus an empty inbox; it does not fabricate sample bookmarks.
states.error: Local storage cannot be read or written: a banner states that the library is unavailable or unsaved and offers retry; it never presents stale data as current.
states.forbidden: Not applicable: the product has exactly one owner role and no shared or public view, so no other role can be denied access here.
states.loading: A first-load state explains that the local library is being read and shows a placeholder list without inventing records.
states.no_results: A search or collection scope yields no records: the view names the active query and collection and offers to clear the search or switch collection.

surfaces.name: Add or edit bookmark
surfaces.purpose: Collect the minimum needed to save a link quickly, optionally pull page details, choose or create a collection, and save or update one record without leaving the library.

query.bulk: Not applicable: only one record can be saved or edited per submission.
query.export: Not applicable: the form neither imports nor exports data.
query.filter: Not applicable: there is no result set to filter; the collection selector is an input choice, not a filter.
query.pagination: Not applicable: the form edits one record at a time.
query.search: Not applicable: the capture form is not a search surface and has no result query.
query.sort: Not applicable: form fields are presented in a fixed task order.

sections: Heading that distinguishes adding from editing
URL field with metadata-fetch action and validation message
Title field with automatic fallback to hostname
Optional description field
Optional tags input
Collection selector with inline create-new option, defaulting to the inbox
Submit and cancel actions

states.empty: A new save form starts blank except for the default inbox selection and a URL placeholder; there are no pre-filled sample records or invented collections.
states.error: Validation errors appear inline next to the fields; a storage failure appears as a form-level error with the values retained.
states.forbidden: Not applicable: only the owner can reach the capture surface, so no permission-denied state exists.
states.loading: While metadata is being fetched, the form remains open with a progress indicator and the owner's entered values preserved; manual entry is still possible.
states.no_results: Not applicable: this is a form rather than a result list, so it has no search-result emptiness; absent metadata is shown as an empty optional field.

surfaces.name: Organization sidebar
surfaces.purpose: Act as the library's structural map: expose the inbox and every user-created collection with counts, support browsing into one, and allow creating or renaming collections.

query.bulk: Not applicable: collection operations act on one collection at a time.
query.export: Not applicable: the sidebar has no export action.
query.filter: Not applicable: it exposes all collections; narrowing happens in the library list.
query.pagination: Not applicable at the boundary's scale; the collection count is small and no paging is defined.
query.search: Not applicable: the sidebar is a short structural list, not a searchable result set.
query.sort: Collections follow a stable sidebar order; locale-dependent names are not re-ranked by the free-text query.

sections: Default inbox entry with record count
User-created collection list ordered by creation or name with record counts
Create-collection control and name validation
Rename control for non-default collections

states.empty: Only the default inbox exists; the sidebar explains that the owner may create the first collection and offers the create control.
states.error: Collections cannot be read: the sidebar shows an error with retry and the library falls back to the inbox only.
states.forbidden: Not applicable: there is no non-owner role and no sharing, so no collection is hidden for permission reasons.
states.loading: The sidebar shows a compact placeholder until collections are read from local storage.
states.no_results: Not applicable: an empty collection is a valid destination and is shown with a zero count rather than treated as a failed result.

surfaces.name: Record detail
surfaces.purpose: Show one record's full identity and metadata, with the primary action of returning to the live page and the ability to edit or move the record.

query.bulk: Not applicable: actions apply to the selected record only.
query.export: Not applicable: no export action exists on the record detail.
query.filter: Not applicable: there is no result set to filter, only a collection assignment to change.
query.pagination: Not applicable: one record is shown at a time.
query.search: Not applicable: the detail view shows one record; search belongs to the library surface.
query.sort: Not applicable: a single record has no ordering.

sections: Title, hostname, and favicon
Full URL with open action
Description and tags
Current collection and move control
Created and last-opened timestamps plus optional open count

states.empty: Not applicable: the detail surface only opens for an existing record, so there is no empty-record variant.
states.error: If the record is no longer present in local storage, the panel closes with a notice and the library refreshes.
states.forbidden: Not applicable: only the single owner can open a record, and no record is shared or restricted.
states.loading: Not applicable in the core because the record is already in the local in-memory list; if a refresh is required, a short loading label is shown rather than a blank panel.
states.no_results: Not applicable: the surface presents one selected record and has no result set.
